mentl/ede1288:
Priority served: the banked next probe of the ADD half of
Hb.effects.feedback-row-substitutes -- read emit's LFeedback arm and decide
whether the constructed spec is dead.

IT IS DEAD, AND THE PROBE VINDICATED THE DOC. Emit destructures the lowered
spec as _spec and discards it. The compiled WAT for a Delay(N) recurrence
contains ZERO construction of it across 1553 lines, and the prior rides a
declared global $__fb_prev_<h>. So the slots really are declared and never
allocated, exactly as SYNTAX §`<~` said; the "untested rather than refuted"
hedge from two iterations ago resolves in the doc's favour, and I have
trued the sentence to say so.

WHAT CHARGES Alloc is infer_expr walking the RHS as an ordinary constructor
call, at a site whose only load-bearing content -- the depth -- is read
statically by feedback_line_depth. The value is lowered, walked by four
pre-passes, and dropped at emit: dead machinery by the loop's own definition.

A GENUINE FORK, BANKED FOR MORGAN rather than answered here, because the
surface and the emit disagree about what a `<~` RHS IS and no measurement
can settle that.

  A. It stays a VALUE, as SYNTAX says today. The fix is narrow -- the `<~`
     arm stops charging the RHS construction and !Alloc survives a cycle.
     One infer site, surface unchanged, and the dead lowering stays.

  B. It becomes a static depth ANNOTATION, which is what emit already
     treats it as. lower_expr(right) and the four walks over the spec
     delete, and the charge disappears with the construction rather than by
     suppression. Cost: the grammar gains a non-expression slot, the thing
     Governing principles spends effort avoiding, and every state-element
     form has to fit it.

B is the smaller artifact and the larger surface change; A is the reverse.

true-up and a priced fork.

mentl/ed31a8c:
The wheel's build_param_types and the seed's pre-registration both DISCARDED the
declared param type (read it as `_`), rebuilding with a fresh placeholder TVar —
so `name: String` and every annotation (refinements, repr pins, ownership) was
inert; the registered signature was always fully polymorphic.

Apply the declared concrete type when present. A bare TVar (unannotated, or a
type-param `x: a`) keeps the fresh placeholder, so HM is preserved for the
un-pinned case. This makes env_find's `name: String` real: `k == name` resolves
to str_eq, not polymorphic pointer-eq, so env_lookup matches the handler-arm op
by VALUE.

MEASURED (m2->m3): env_find emits `call $str_eq` (op-key) + `i32.eq` (len==0
check); `wat_emit` op-miss 1->0 — the op-lookup gating register_handler RESOLVES;
the trap marches off op-resolution into the evidence/ev-slot layer
(op_each_handler_yield call_indirect). 24/24 micros green, no regression.

Carried in the same fix (ultimate form):
- bind_pat_locals threads the destructure element's type handle + a tuple-type
  chase (both layers; the seed mirrors the wheel's tuple_pat_strip), so a
  destructure-bound String local's `==` dispatches structurally.
- `==` consults BOTH operands: str_eq if either side resolves to a sequence,
  never silent pointer-eq for a known sequence.

Named peer: Hβ.eq.polymorphic-structural-via-evidence — a genuinely polymorphic
`==` (both operands free) still floors to i32.eq; the structural fold via runtime
evidence is the unsurpassable form.

perennials/edf30d7:
The sheet asked her to redraw her own yard from memory: beds she could
photograph from the porch had to be traced freehand onto blank paper, and a
placement's position meant nothing except relative to the rest of the ink.
Now a yard can hold one photo of the ground, and her ink draws over it.

Only the key rides in the yard record. The image goes through the same door
as her plant photos (shrunk to 1400px, into IndexedDB), because an image in
localStorage would eat the 5MB lane that keeps a hundred yards safe. On
screen the photo is washed to near-grey at half opacity, which is tokens.css
doing double duty: saturated colour keeps meaning plant data, and a faded
print is also what sepia ink stays legible on.

The photo is the paper, not a stroke. Setting or removing it skips the undo
stack, and undo carries the live ground forward, so undoing past a photo
change can neither resurrect a deleted key as a hole in the sheet nor detach
a ground she just laid. That rule is also what makes the eager blob delete
safe: no snapshot can bring a dropped key back.

The backup now collects every key her stores point at, not every key her
mine records point at. Two stores hold photo keys now, so the collection is
one pure function, photoKeys, and rules.test.ts watches it. Deleting a yard
deletes its ground, the bargain mine.ts already makes for a plant photo.

The shared sheet carries the ground, washed the same way. The old rule kept
photographs out for taint and offline reasons, and both are about source
images fetched over the network; hers is a local blob riding as a data URL,
which taints nothing and needs no signal.
noodles/edbd23d:
The loop bar drove live playback but export ignored it — you could set
the perfect 4-bar loop, hear it cycle, then export and get the whole
arrangement instead. The two halves of scenario 2 (throw down a loop,
play it through the room) didn't talk.

Now the loop IS the backing track. When a loop is set, the export sheet
leads with "Export loop · N bars"; master and stems sit below. The
render is seamless: renderOffline(null, {loop}) plays the region twice
and keeps the second cycle (sliceBuffer), so the first pass's reverb/
echo/release tail bleeds into the second's downbeat and the file wraps
into itself with no click when any looper repeats it. Full-arrangement
and stem exports are unchanged (the render path is now shared).

Verified: 2 bars @120 renders exactly 4.000s, peak -0.2, the head
carries the wrapped tail (-4.1dB, not a bare cut); the loop-first button
appears only when loop.on and saves noodles-loop.wav.
noodles/edfd324:
The loop brace was a 9 px sliver with one invisible right-edge handle.
The ruler now splits in two: bar numbers and playhead taps on top, a
26 px loop lane underneath where every gesture belongs to the loop —
drag the body to move it, grab either visible edge grip to resize
either end, tap the brace to toggle it, drag across empty lane space
to paint a new loop right there (auto-enabled), and tap empty space to
bring the loop to that bar with its length kept. Edits snap to bars,
the start edge can't cross the end, and undo captures only committed
changes instead of every touch. Smoke paints a loop and toggles it
off through the real pointer paths.
noodles/edf51cb:
Builder report from an 8-inch speaker: a roll dealt the deep preset a
C1 bassline and nothing came through — deep is a driveless sine, and a
33 Hz fundamental has no harmonics for a small cone to carry. Popping
it an octave up fixed it, so that is literally the rule now: fresh
magic basslines fold up an octave when deep is the rolled preset.
Presets with drive keep their octave-1 rolls (their harmonics land at
66/99 Hz and read fine), and hand-placed low notes stay untouched —
that is exploration, not a deal from the house. Smoke rolls the dice
six extra times and holds the invariant.
bits/ed7cbcd:
The plan's done condition was the audit's own table, measured again in
the same units. It is re-taken, and not by eye: the walkthrough now
records every number in the same run that asserts on it, writes
dist-ux-shots/measurements.md, and the audit's section 7 carries both
columns. The worst overlay over the stage went from 83% to 20%, and from
100% to 9% with a puppet selected. The timeline went from 74px with an
invisible scrubber to 216px with a 48px touch target and a visible
handle. A hold on a puppet went from one DROP to nothing. Sending a
puppet back went from N events to one. Nothing lands above the top of a
375x667 screen any more, where the kit's header used to sit 123px out of
reach.

Measuring it turned up a real bug. The halo and the handles are
positioned by the frame loop, which only lays out when something has
dirtied the canvas — so a selection arriving any other way (a sheet
closing, a cast landing, undo) left the bar at the stage's top-left
corner, on top of the title strip, until the next redraw. It is
positioned in a layout effect now, before paint, which also removes the
one-frame flash on every selection. The walkthrough caught it because
taps now refuse to land on something else: it reported the back button
as covered by a mouth.

Two new assertions (nothing off the top of a small phone, the foley row
fits), fresh screenshots under docs/ux-audit/shots-now/, and a status
line on the plan saying what is built and what is not: the iPhone pass,
which was never schedulable and still has not happened.
